To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

nutrition education intervention research trials are often not designed to provide sufficient evidence to determine whether behavioral or cognition changes are attributed to the intervention, because the experimental design often includes an inactive control condition or does not report sufficient details to allow for replication of the nutrition intervention studied.
the control groups of nutrition education intervention research studies are rarely described in enough detail to permit replication of their treatments.

the majority of nutrition education intervention trials in peer-reviewed literature have active control conditions, but many of these studies fail to report one or several key elements of the nutrition education intervention.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quality of the research that is being published in peer-reviewed journals.

the following: (1) identifying the most effective nutrition education interventions to promote positive dietary and physical activity behavior changes in the United States, (2) understanding how to implement these interventions in real-world settings, (3) identifying factors that may contribute to intervention effectiveness, (4) determining how to disseminate and scale up evidence-based interventions to promote population-level changes, (5) identifying gaps in the research literature, and (6) identifying opportunities for future research.
the quality of the control group in nutrition education interventions, and the implications for the validity of study outcomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is insufficient evidence to support the efficacy of any nutrition education intervention because of the weak study designs and lack of reporting of key elements.
there is insufficient evidence to determine whether nutrition education interventions are effective.
there is insufficient evidence in the reviewed studies to determine whether nutrition education interventions can improve dietary intake and related health outcomes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the control groups in these studies were often poorly defined, which may have contributed to the lack of replication of the interventions.
there is a need for more complete reporting of the interventions in the control group, as well as in the intervention group.
the quality of control groups in intervention studies is inconsistent and needs to be strengthened.
The main takeaway from our work is that
researchers must be transparent about the control condition and rationale for selecting the control condition, and report key elements of the experimental and comparison conditions.
the control group treatment should be as similar as possible to the treatment in the experimental group.
researchers should consider the type of control condition that best suits their research question, as it can have a significant impact on study results.
